Yes, the cable can cap your charging speed. Your charger and device set the ceiling, and the cable can only lower it.

**How the ratings work**
- **60W cables** carry up to 20V at 3A. Most USB-C cables are in this class, and they don't need an e-marker chip.
- **100W cables** carry 20V at 5A and need an e-marker chip. USB-IF stopped certifying new 100W cables on December 22, 2021, and replaced them with 240W (48V, 5A). Many 100W cables are still sold, but they're no longer a certified category. ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations), [USB-IF compliance updates](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?Format=Standard&UpdateFile=Cables+and+Connectors&pubDate=20261005))
- **240W cables** use the Extended Power Range (EPR) spec, which requires an e-marker and the 240W logo. They also support the 28V, 36V and 48V steps that give 140W, 180W and 240W. ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd))

Under the current USB-IF rules, certified USB-C to USB-C cables are labeled either 60W or 240W.

**When it matters**
- **Phones, earbuds, tablets under about 60W:** a 60W cable is fine.
- **Laptops drawing 65-100W:** you need a 5A, e-marked cable, which means a "100W" or 240W cable. A 60W cable will limit you to about 60W.
- **Laptops or devices above 100W:** you need a 240W EPR cable, plus a charger and device that support it.

The USB-IF also notes that a certified cable doesn't add capability to the charger or device ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)). A 240W cable on a 30W charger still gives 30W.

**Check your own cable:** look for a wattage logo on the connector or packaging. A cable with no markings is safest to assume is 60W or lower. Cable data speed is separate from power. Some 240W cables are USB 2.0 only (480 Mbps), which is fine for charging but slow for data.

**If you need a 100W cable:** the Baseus USB-C to USB-C cable is e-marked at 5A and costs $9.99 for 1 m, with 2 m at $12.99 and 3 m at $16.99. Its limits are that it's USB 2.0 data only, has no video output, and isn't rated for 140W or 240W. Baseus also says it isn't supported for iPad Pro charging. ([Buy at Baseus](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w), [details](https://dealectric.com/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w)). That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you buy through it.

**If you need 240W:** the search results list USB-IF certified 240W cables, such as the Bonelk Easy grip USB-C to USB-C (240W, 480 Mbps, 6 ft) and a Luxshare 80Gbps 240W cable ([USB-IF certified product list](https://www.usb.org/products)). They didn't include retail links or prices, so I can't point you to a place to buy them from these results.

If you tell me which charger and device you're using, I can say which rating you actually need.
